headline: Hasan Mahmud's 6-55 bowls Australia out for 198 in Darwin
summary: Bangladesh seized the honours on Day 1 of the Test, with Hasan Mahmud claiming a career-best 6-55 to dismantle the Australian side.
details: Hasan Mahmud delivered a masterclass in pace bowling, claiming a career-best 6-55 to bowl Australia out for 198. This performance marks the first time a Bangladesh bowler has taken a five-for in Australia across all formats.
Australia's total of 198 is their lowest Test score against Bangladesh, surpassing the previous low of 217 recorded in the 2017 Mirpur Test.
Hasan's feat makes him only the third Bangladesh bowler to achieve a Test five-for against Australia, joining Mohammad Rafique and Shakib Al Hasan.
Bangladesh responded with a strong start, closing the first day at 96-1, just 102 runs behind. Mominul Haque remained unbeaten on 35 and Tanzid Hasan on 32.
In a historic milestone, Mominul Haque surpassed Tamim Iqbal to become Bangladesh's second-highest Test run-scorer, moving behind only Mushfiqur Rahim.
The match also saw Mitchell Starc become the most successful left-arm bowler in Test history, surpassing Sri Lanka's Rangana Herath with 434 wickets.
Notably, this was only the second time Bangladesh's pacers took all 10 wickets in a Test innings, a feat previously achieved against Pakistan in Rawalpindi in 2024.

headline: DU to investigate 58 teachers for alleged anti-state activities
summary: A three-member committee has been formed to examine claims that some faculty members were involved in secret activities to bring back ousted PM Sheikh Hasina.
details: Dhaka University has formed a three-member committee to investigate allegations that several of its teachers were involved in "secret activities against the state".
The committee is headed by Pro-Vice Chancellor (Education) Prof Dr Abdus Salam, with members including the deans of the Faculty of Science and the Faculty of Law.
The move follows media reports claiming that 404 teachers from 22 universities were involved in activities aimed at bringing back ousted Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina.
These reports also alleged that the university teachers were attempting to activate a political party that is currently banned in the country.
While the reports identified 92 DU teachers, the university administration has so far identified 58 of them.
The committee will review the cases of these 58 teachers and make recommendations for necessary action. They will also review any additional names that may emerge.
The university has not yet disclosed the names of the teachers under investigation.
